kaps_punt: Kindermishandeling: Verskillende vorme van kindermishandeling: fisies en emosioneel; Effek van mishandeling op persoonlike gesondheid; Strategiee om mishandeling te hanteer; en Waar om hulp te vind en mishandeling aan te meld.

items.bewering: Party grootmense maak 'n kind aspris seer. Ander behandel 'n kind so sleg dat dit hom skade aandoen. Albei is kindermishandeling.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1, definition of 'abuse': 'any form of harm or ill-treatment deliberately inflicted on a child' (Acts Online, https://www.acts.co.za/childrens-act-2005/1_interpretation). Harm and ill-treatment map onto the two sentences.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens of 'n ander kind kan dit doen.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s1 'abuse' para (c): 'bullying by another child' (Acts Online, https://www.acts.co.za/childrens-act-2005/1_interpretation); also Centre for Child Law, https://www.centreforchildlaw.co.za/2025/10/the-centre-for-child-law-condemns-the-incident-of-bullying-at-milnerton-high-school/

items.bewering: Mishandeling gebeur nooit per ongeluk nie en lyk nie altyd dieselfde nie.
items.bron: Children's Act s1: abuse is harm 'deliberately inflicted'; paras (a)-(e) list several different forms. Jamieson & Mahery, 'A Guide to the Children's Act ... Part 2', Child and Youth Care Work 28(6), 2010 (UCT open repository, https://open.uct.ac.za/bitstreams/391b48b2-9eba-45db-b638-6a61a7bec334/download), notes an accidental injury falls outside s110 because it was not inflicted by another person. The absolute 'nooit' holds under the legal definition.

items.bewering: Fisiese mishandeling is wanneer iemand 'n kind se liggaam aspris seermaak, soos om hom te slaan, skop, brand of gooi.
items.bron: NSPCC, Physical abuse (https://www.nspcc.org.uk/keeping-children-safe/types-of-abuse/physical-abuse/): hurting a child on purpose, examples include hitting, kicking, throwing, burning and scalding. Children's Act s1 'abuse' para (a): assault or any other deliberate injury.

items.bewering: Dit laat soms 'n merk.
items.bron: Jamieson & Mahery 2010 (UCT), quoting the Children's Act regulations' indicators of physical abuse: bruises, grasp marks, belt marks, burn marks, cuts, welts. 'Soms' is correct: not every assault leaves a visible mark.

items.bewering: Emosionele mishandeling gebeur met woorde en dade. Oor en oor skel iemand 'n kind uit, kleineer hom, maak hom bang of laat hom ongewens voel.
items.bron: NSPCC, Emotional abuse (https://www.nspcc.org.uk/what-is-child-abuse/types-of-abuse/emotional-abuse/): 'continual emotional mistreatment', including humiliating, constantly criticising, threatening, shouting and deliberately trying to scare a child. Children's Act s1 'abuse' para (e): behaviour that may harm the child psychologically or emotionally.

items.bewering: Dit laat geen merk op die liggaam nie. Dit is steeds mishandeling en doen skade.
items.bron: NSPCC Emotional abuse page: it is often hard to recognise and can show few outward signs, and its effects include anxiety, depression and lack of confidence. Children's Act s1 para (e) counts it as abuse.

items.bewering: Mishandeling raak 'n kind se gesondheid en nie net sy liggaam nie.
items.bron: NSPCC Emotional abuse page, on effects: mental health problems including depression and anxiety, and eating problems.

items.bewering: Sommige kinders wat mishandel word, slaap sleg of eet sleg. Party voel baie bang, en ander voel kwaad vir die mense rondom hulle. Party sukkel om by die skool te konsentreer of bly van ander kinders af weg.
items.bron: Nationwide Children's Hospital, 'Signs of child abuse' (https://www.nationwidechildrens.org/-/media/nch/700childrens/2022/04/signs-of-child-abuse-pdf.pdf): nightmares or difficulty falling asleep, changed eating, difficulty concentrating in school, scared, withdrawn or more aggressive. The Children's Act regulations' indicators (quoted in Jamieson & Mahery 2010) also list persistent fear, aggression and withdrawal. 'Sommige' and 'party' are correctly hedged.

items.bewering: Nie een van hierdie tekens beteken op sy eie dat 'n kind mishandel word nie.
items.bron: City of London, 'Worried about a child' (https://www.fis.cityoflondon.gov.uk/asset-library/worried-about-a-child1.pdf): these signs do not necessarily mean a child is being abused, and changes may have other causes. Jamieson & Mahery 2010: a conclusion must rest on the 'total context', not on one indicator.

items.bewering: Mishandeling is nooit die kind se skuld nie. Dit bly waar al sê die grootmens die kind het dit verdien. Dit bly waar al was die kind stout of ongehoorsaam.
items.blok: Dit is nooit die kind se skuld nie
items.bron: Children's Commissioner for England, 'Young Person's Guide to Keeping Children Safe' (https://assets.childrenscommissioner.gov.uk/wpuploads/2017/07/GUIDE_Young_Persons_Guide_to_Keeping_Children_Safe.pdf): adults who abuse children are responsible for their actions, not the child. US Office for Victims of Crime (https://ovc.ojp.gov/sites/ovc/files/pubs/OVC_Archives/reports/help_series/pdftxt/whatyoushouldknow6_11.txt): the adult is to blame even when they tell the child it is the child's fault.

items.bewering: 'n Grootmens wat 'n kind seermaak, het self so gekies. Om die mishandeling stop te sit is die werk van ander grootmense en nie die kind s'n nie.
items.blok: Dit is nooit die kind se skuld nie
items.bron: Children's Act s1 ('deliberately inflicted') and s110 (the duty to act lies with listed adult professionals). Children's Commissioner guide: abusers know what they are doing and are responsible.

items.bewering: Die belangrikste is om dit te vertel.
items.blok: Vertel dit vir iemand wat jy vertrou
items.bron: This is the central advice in child-safety guidance: OCRCC body-safety lesson (https://ocrcc.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/CAREGIVERS_-PreK-1st-Safe-Touch-lesson-review-.pdf) and the Children's Commissioner guide both put telling a trusted adult first. The superlative is advice, not a ranked fact, and the guidance supports it.

items.bewering: Kies 'n volwassene wat jy vertrou, soos 'n onderwyser of 'n ouma. As daardie een nie luister of help nie, vertel 'n ander volwassene wat jy vertrou. Hou aan tot iemand help.

items.bron: Texas A&M COPS child-safety handout (https://reslife.tamu.edu/wp-content/uploads/COPS_CHILD_SAFETY_K5.pdf): keep telling until someone listens. Australian school child-safe resource (https://www.shcgeelong.catholic.edu.au/uploads/Files/ChildSafeStandard_FeelingSafeSecondarySchool1-2.pdf): if one adult cannot help, keep trying until one can.

items.bewering: 'n Geheim wat jou bang maak, is nie 'n geheim wat jy hoef te hou nie.

items.bron: Texas A&M COPS handout: an abuser may demand secrecy, and breaking that promise is acceptable. US OVC guide: never keep it secret, even if threatened.

items.bewering: As dit veilig is, mag jy 'Nee' sê en weggaan, ook vir 'n grootmens by die huis. Is dit nie veilig nie, gaan na 'n veilige plek of ander mense. Kon jy nie nee sê of wegkom nie, het jy niks verkeerd gedoen nie. Vertel daarna altyd iemand.

items.bron: 'No, Go, Tell' body-safety rule (Vaestoliitto, https://www.vaestoliitto.fi/en/articles/how-to-teach-safety-skills-to-children/; The News Minute, https://www.thenewsminute.com/article/no-go-tell-watch-actor-nivin-pauly-talk-children-about-child-body-safety-60889). OCRCC: abuse is never the child's fault even if the child did not manage the safety steps. The lesson's 'if it is safe' condition is a correct safety qualifier.

items.bewering: Moenie later teruggaan om die persoon daaroor aan te spreek of te stry nie, grootmens of kind. Om dit verder te neem is die werk van grootmense soos onderwysers, maatskaplike werkers en die polisie.

items.bron: This is safety advice. The body-safety sources (OCRCC, Texas A&M COPS) send the child to an adult and never to confront the person. Children's Act s110 (Jamieson & Mahery 2010) gives the reporting duty to teachers, social workers and others, and reports go to the police, Social Development or a child-protection organisation. No source found contradicts the advice.

items.bewering: Kindermishandeling is teen die wet in Suid-Afrika.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005, s305(3) makes abuse or deliberate neglect of a child by a parent, guardian or caregiver an offence, punishable by a fine or up to 10 years' imprisonment under s305(6) (Acts Online, https://www.acts.co.za/childrens-act-2005/305_offences; applied in S v JR 2015 (2) SACR 162 (GP)). Assault is also a crime.

items.bewering: Die wet sê onderwysers en susters by die kliniek moet dit aanmeld as hulle glo 'n kind is so mishandel dat hy beseer is.
items.bron: Children's Act s110(1), quoted in full in Jamieson & Mahery 2010 (Children's Institute, UCT open repository): '...nurse ... teacher ... who on reasonable grounds concludes that a child has been abused in a manner causing physical injury, sexually abused or deliberately neglected, must report that conclusion...'. Teachers and nurses are both named and the physical-injury condition matches. 'Glo' simplifies 'on reasonable grounds concludes', which is acceptable for Grade 5. The duty also covers sexual abuse and deliberate neglect, which the lesson leaves out. That is incomplete, not false.

items.bron: Childline South Africa home page (https://www.childlinesa.org.za), read 23 October 2026: '24 hour Toll-free Number on 116', 'Call us 24/7 - we are free from all networks'. Vuk'uzenzele (government), November 2021 (https://www.vukuzenzele.gov.za/children-can-call-116-help): children can dial 116 themselves. The lesson gives no number, so the number cannot go stale here.

items.bewering: Childline hou wat jy vertel privaat, behalwe as hulle dink jy is in gevaar of meer hulp nodig het. Dan kan hulle 'n maatskaplike werker of die polisie inbring.
items.bron: Findahelpline listing for Childline South Africa (https://findahelpline.com/organizations/childline-south-africa): 'free and confidential'. Vuk'uzenzele (government), November 2021: 'If necessary, Childline will refer them to the police and/or a social worker at the Department of Social Development'. Paarl Post (https://novanews.co.za/paarlpost/?p=51127): emergency cases go to social workers and the police. I did not find Childline SA's own written confidentiality policy. The lesson's broad wording ('in gevaar of meer hulp nodig het') matches the published 'if necessary' referral practice and does not claim a narrower threshold.

items.bewering: 'n Volwassene kan ook help om te bel. Jy kan ook vertel as dit met 'n ander kind gebeur.
items.bron: Vuk'uzenzele, November 2021: 'By dialing 116, children and adults can receive help with problems facing children.' Wikipedia, Childline South Africa (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childline_South_Africa): the service is for children and for adults with concerns about children.

items.bewering: Mense wat kan help: 'n onderwyser of die skoolhoof; 'n maatskaplike werker wat kinders en gesinne help; 'n suster by die kliniek; die polisie by die naaste polisiestasie; Childline se hulplyn wat jy self gratis kan bel, dag en nag.
items.bron: Children's Act s110(1) (Jamieson & Mahery 2010): teachers, nurses and social workers are all mandatory reporters, and reports may go to a police official. Childline SA home page: free, 24 hours.

items.bron: SACSSP, Social Work (https://www.sacssp.co.za/social-work): a regulated, trained profession that works with people to deal with life challenges and improve wellbeing. Children's Act s110 and s150 (Jamieson & Mahery 2010): social workers investigate child-protection cases and work with families.

items.bron: Children's Act s110 and Regulation 33 (reports go to a designated child-protection organisation, Social Development or the police; Jamieson & Mahery 2010). The everyday meaning of 'aanmeld' as reporting to the proper authority fits.

opsomming: All 29 claims check out against South African law (Children's Act s1, s110 and s305), Childline SA's own site, a government publication and established child-protection guidance. There are no analogies, and the one superlative ('Die belangrikste is om dit te vertel') is supported advice. Two points are worth a person's knowing: the teachers-and-nurses reporting sentence names only physical-injury abuse, although the law also covers sexual abuse and deliberate neglect (incomplete, not false), and Childline SA publishes no written confidentiality rule, so the 'privaat, behalwe as' sentence rests on its 'confidential' listing and the government's 'if necessary' referral wording.
